bull_bear.body:
- Positioning of The Leela Mumbai as one of India's leading luxury hospitality destinations, with the hotel commanding a premium over several competitors owing to its location advantage, established service reputation and strong brand association
- Location advantage adjacent to Mumbai airport, supporting demand from premium corporate travellers and airline crew
- International distribution and loyalty reach through Global Hotel Alliance (and its DISCOVERY loyalty programme) and Preferred Hotels & Resorts, plus marketing arrangements through Brookfield for which the Company pays a fee based on marketing expenses
- Global sales-representation network via Preferred Hotels & Resorts engaging tour operators, travel designers and retail agencies in key source markets
- Brand recognition evidenced by the Tripadvisor 2026 Travelers' Choice Award and five ET Restaurant & Nightlife Awards 2026 nominations across its dining outlets
- Association with the broader expansion momentum of The Leela group, expected to strengthen network visibility and brand depth
- Captive renewable generation (3 windmills of 4.5 MW plus 230 KW rooftop solar) reducing purchased-power dependence
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-asset / single-city concentration — Management states the Company 'continues to face concentration risk arising from heavy dependence on one hotel in Mumbai and exposure to the upper luxury segment' — the entire business is The Leela Mumbai, so any local demand, supply or asset-specific shock is unmitigated by diversification. (Back-filled from the MD&A text delivered in the strategy_outlook bundle; the risks_esg bundle received Directors' Report governance sections instead.)
- Airline-crew demand migration to the Navi Mumbai airport ecosystem — The Crew segment remained an important contributor, benefiting from Mumbai's position as one of India's busiest aviation hubs, but the ongoing redevelopment and expansion of Terminal 1 at Mumbai Airport together with the commencement of operations at Navi Mumbai International Airport is expected to gradually alter airline operating patterns and crew accommodation requirements, with a portion of crew demand potentially migrating to hotels in the Navi Mumbai micro-market. This is a structural, dated demand risk to a named revenue segment. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A text.)
- Land tenure and lease-rental dispute with Airports Authority of India — Ongoing disputes over what the Company calls the exorbitant demand of lease rental and royalty in the form of Minimum Guaranteed Amount on the hotel land of 18,000 sq. meters and adjacent land of 11,000 sq. meters, including AAI eviction proceedings. Per the Bombay High Court judgment of June 09, 2025 the lease-rental dispute continues before the AAI Eviction Officer while FSI utilisation, land amalgamation and damages go to arbitration before retired Justice Mr. S.V. Gangapurwala. Renewal of the 18,000 sq. meter lease (the Company has accepted AAI's offer letter dated December 01, 2023 and sought a further 30 years) is still awaited — the site the sole hotel stands on is therefore not on secure long-term tenure. (Back-filled from the Directors' Report text delivered in the profile bundle.)
- Unresolved shareholder litigation over the Brookfield transaction — ITC Limited and Russell Credit Limited (holding then 8.72%, at present 8.10%) have a Section 241/242/244 oppression-and-mismanagement petition pending, with the Company and promoters Mr. Vivek Nair and Mr. Dinesh Nair appealing the NCLT Mumbai waiver order of January 24, 2024 before the NCLAT, Delhi; ITC's further appeal against the SEBI order (which favoured the Company on July 23, 2019) and the SAT dismissal of September 26, 2019 is pending before the Supreme Court of India. A minority-shareholder overhang on the Company's largest corporate action. (Back-filled from the Directors' Report text delivered in the profile bundle.)
- Macroeconomic, geopolitical and travel-corridor sensitivity — The hotel business continues to be dependent on domestic and global economic conditions, airline connectivity, consumer confidence and the overall geopolitical environment; ongoing geopolitical tensions in conflict-affected regions, trade disruptions, energy-price and crude-oil volatility, airfare volatility, changing travel corridors and inflationary pressure on discretionary spending may influence travel flows, operating costs and discretionary spending. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A text.)
- Occupancy erosion despite rate-led growth — FY 2025-26 occupancy fell to 69% from 73.80% in FY 2024-25, with revenue growth carried by ARR (Rs. 12,469 vs Rs. 11,170) and RevPAR (Rs. 8,602 vs Rs. 8,242); management describes revenue growth as achieved 'despite lower overall room inventory utilisation', and notes that protecting occupancy, average room rates and revenue quality requires sustained sales agility in an environment of geopolitical uncertainty, changing travel behaviour and higher guest expectations. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A Business Review.)
- Cyber, information-security and business-continuity risk — The MD&A cites elevated cyber and security concerns in the global operating environment, and the Board-approved Risk Management Policy framework expressly covers financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability, information and cyber security risks, with measures for risk mitigation including systems and processes for internal control of identified risks and a business continuity plan.
- Audit observations on the financial statements — The Directors' Report states that although there are no audit qualifications or adverse remarks, there ARE audit observations on the financial statements, with the explanation given in Notes 37.1 and 37.3 — a standing accounting/disclosure watch-item. The routed text does not reproduce the substance of those notes.

business.body: HLV Limited is engaged in the hotel business and, for regulatory purposes, is classified as providing 'infrastructure facilities' under Schedule VI to the Companies Act. Its operations consist of a single luxury hotel, The Leela Mumbai (Sahar, Mumbai), serving premium corporate travellers, retail guests, airline crew, social celebrations and international visitors, together with its restaurant and banqueting offerings. The Company states there has been no fundamental change in the nature of its business during the year ended March 31, 2026, and that it is a service industry without significant manufacturing operations.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Sustain the positioning of The Leela Mumbai as one of India's leading luxury hospitality destinations, driving rate-led revenue growth (ARR improved to Rs. 12,469 from Rs. 11,170, growth of over 12%) rather than volume
- Continued focus on revenue optimisation and quality business mix, reflected in RevPAR improving to Rs. 8,602 from Rs. 8,242
- Maintain alliance-based international reach through Global Hotel Alliance (and its DISCOVERY loyalty programme) and Preferred Hotels & Resorts for loyalty-led demand generation, global sales representation and access to affluent international travellers
- Continue marketing arrangements through Brookfield, for which the Company pays a fee based on the marketing expenses, to support international visibility and premium market access
- Continue availing sales, marketing and PR representation companies across important geographies through Preferred Hotels & Resorts to engage tour operators, travel designers and retail agencies in source markets
- Sustained focus on service excellence, direct demand generation and relationship-led selling to protect occupancy, average room rates and revenue quality
- Maintain a robust risk management framework to identify, assess and mitigate potential threats (description truncated in the routed text)
- The Company declared no dividend for FY 2025-26 ('Your directors do not recommend any dividend for the year ended March 31, 2026') and the Board decided to retain the entire amount of FY 2025-26 profit appearing in the Statement of Profit and Loss, i.e. full retention with no transfer to a separate reserve. No securities were issued or allotted during the year, and the report expressly states there were no issues of differential-rights equity, sweat equity, employee share schemes, employee stock options, employee-benefit trusts, debentures/bonds/convertible securities or warrants, and no deposits accepted or renewed under Section 73. Being classified as providing 'infrastructure facilities' under Schedule VI, the Company is exempt from Section 186 compliance for loans, guarantees and security, so no such particulars are disclosed. No buyback, debt-reduction target or credit rating is stated in the routed text.
- Energy conservation and 'Green' hotel drive stated as the main focus through the year: extensive installation of LED and energy-efficient electrical equipment; high-efficiency HVAC systems used/retrofitted extensively, which have reduced electrical consumption; computerized power monitoring implemented to monitor and control power consumption; main chiller plants and steam boilers tuned for best efficiency
- Captive renewable power: 3 windmills with a capacity of 4.5 MW in the State of Maharashtra, continuing to produce renewable energy for use in the Company's own hotel
- Rooftop solar: 230 KW solar panels installed and commissioned on the building rooftop to maximise utilisation of renewable power
- Heat and water recovery: condensate recovery unit for generating hot water, and energy-saving devices in guest rooms during non-occupancy
- Water and plastic reduction: in-house recycled drinking water glass bottling plant catering to all guest rooms and restaurants; STP-treated water used for the cooling tower and garden; rainwater harvesting implemented
- CSR: Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 applies to the Company, but because the amount required to be spent during the financial year does not exceed Rs. 50 lakh, a CSR Committee is not required under Section 135(9) and the CSR functions are discharged by the Board itself; the CSR Policy is published on the Company's website and the year's initiatives are set out in Annexure II
- POSH: zero-tolerance policy covering all permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees, with an Internal Complaints Committee constituted; status as on March 31, 2026 — 01 complaint filed during the year, 01 disposed of during the year, NIL pending at year-end
- Whistle Blower Policy / Vigil Mechanism in place for directors and employees to report genuine concerns or grievances
- Risk governance: a Risk Management Committee formed by the Board to frame, implement and monitor the risk management plan and policy, with the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risks and controls; the policy framework explicitly includes sustainability risk

outlook.body: The routed text discloses NO hotel capacity addition, new-property or expansion project by the Company itself — HLV Limited remains a single-hotel operator (The Leela Mumbai) and states there has been no fundamental change in the nature of its business during FY 2025-26. The only asset-side additions disclosed are energy assets and efficiency retrofits described under Conservation of Energy: the Company has 3 windmills with a capacity of 4.5 MW power in the State of Maharashtra which continue to produce renewable energy for use in its own hotel, and it has 'installed and commission 230 KW Solar panels on the building rooftop' for renewable solar generation. Other in-hotel investments described are extensive LED and energy-efficient electrical equipment, high-efficiency HVAC systems used/retrofitted extensively, computerized power monitoring, tuning of main chiller plants and steam boilers, a condensate recovery unit for hot water, energy-saving devices in rooms during non-occupancy, an in-house recycled drinking water glass bottling plant serving all guest rooms and restaurants, STP-treated water for cooling tower/garden, and rainwater harvesting. On the property footprint, the Company's hotel land of 18,000 sq. meters and adjacent land of 11,000 sq. meters are held on lease from the Airports Authority of India; the Company has accepted AAI's offer letter dated December 01, 2023 for renewal of the 18,000 sq. meter lease and has requested renewal for a further period of 30 years, with FSI utilisation, land amalgamation and damages referred to arbitration (this land/lease context comes from the profile bundle's Directors' Report text). Technology absorption disclosure is stated to be not applicable as the hotel is a service industry and the Company does not have any significant manufacturing operations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's growth outlook for FY 2025-26 remained robust, with the RBI projecting real GDP growth at 7.4 per cent, supported by strong domestic demand, buoyant services activity and sustained investment momentum
- Global growth projected by the IMF at 3.1 per cent in 2026 following 3.2 per cent in 2025 — slower but still positive expansion amid renewed inflationary pressures and policy uncertainty
- Continued infrastructure development, improving connectivity, rising disposable incomes and sustained consumption across business and leisure segments supporting a favourable demand environment for hospitality and travel-linked sectors
- UN Tourism: international tourist arrivals reached an estimated 1.4 billion in 2024, up 11 per cent over 2023 and equivalent to 99 per cent of pre-pandemic levels; Q1 2025 recorded more than 300 million international travellers, a further 5 per cent increase; arrivals expected to grow around 3 to 5 per cent, a return to more normalised growth
- WTTC: travel and tourism's contribution to global GDP reached approximately US$11.6 trillion to US$11.7 trillion in 2025, about 10.3 per cent of the global economy and a new record above pre-pandemic levels
- Indian hospitality demand drivers: rising domestic tourism, destination weddings, M.I.C.E. activity, spiritual tourism, premium leisure travel, wellness-led travel, business mobility and improved transport infrastructure
- Branded room supply in many markets remained measured relative to demand growth, providing favourable demand-supply dynamics for quality hotel assets with strong brand positioning and location advantage
- FY26 business review: hotel occupancy of 69% versus 73.80% in FY 2024-25, ARR of Rs. 12,469 versus Rs. 11,170 (over 12% growth), RevPAR of Rs. 8,602 versus Rs. 8,242, and total rooms revenue of Rs. 124.96 crore versus Rs. 119.29 crore — rate-led growth despite lower room inventory utilisation
- Demand mix drawn from premium corporate travellers, retail guests, airline crews, social celebrations and international visitors; the Crew segment remained an important contributor, benefiting from Mumbai's position as one of India's busiest aviation hubs
- Watch-item on the demand side: redevelopment and expansion of Terminal 1 at Mumbai Airport plus commencement of operations at Navi Mumbai International Airport are expected to gradually alter airline operating patterns, with a portion of airline crew demand potentially migrating to Navi Mumbai micro-market hotels
- Operating environment remains sensitive to geopolitical developments, conflicts in certain regions, crude oil price volatility, airfare volatility, changing travel corridors and inflation-led pressure on discretionary spending

litigation.note: Two material long-running disputes. (1) ITC Limited and its subsidiary Russell Credit Limited, members holding then 8.72% (at present 8.10%) of equity, filed a petition under Sections 241/242/244 before the NCLT in April 2019 alleging oppression and mismanagement in relation to the Company's transaction with BSREP III India Ballet Pte. Ltd. and affiliates ('Brookfield') for the sale of the Company's hotel undertakings; NCLT Mumbai allowed ITC/Russell Credit's waiver application on January 24, 2024, and the Company together with promoters Mr. Vivek Nair and Mr. Dinesh Nair has appealed to the NCLAT, Delhi, where the matter is being heard. Parallel SEBI complaints by ITC and LIC (LIC later withdrew) resulted in a SEBI order dated July 23, 2019 in favour of the Company; ITC's appeal was dismissed by SAT on September 26, 2019, and ITC's further appeal is pending before the Supreme Court of India. Gangapurwala, with both proceedings currently running. The disputes were also referred to AAI's Settlement Advisory Committee since 2020; the Company received an AAI offer letter dated December 01, 2023 for renewal of the 18,000 sq. meter lease, which it has accepted, and has sought renewal for a further period of 30 years. Amounts are deliberately not reproduced.
